body.statement:
For an admissible fixed choice of class constants with \(H=0\), \(p=S=d=1\), \(\lambda=\kappa=1\), and the uniform order-zero kernel \(K\), there is a triangular array of laws in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\), with \(n_1=N=T^2\), for which
\[
R_\star=T^{-2},\qquad
\lim_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E\!\left[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0\right]=\frac{3}{16}.
\]
In the same array, the event multiplier radius satisfies \(r_{\mathrm{tr}}=0\) almost surely even though the conditional variance of the centered event contribution is \(3/16\).
Moreover, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
body.proof_tex:
It suffices to construct one admissible triangular array.  Fix
\(H=0\), \(p=S=d=1\), \(\lambda=\kappa=1\), and \(\pi _1=1\).  Take
\[
B=16,\qquad c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1,
\qquad \delta _0=\frac14,
\qquad c_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}=1,
\]
and take the H\"older radius \(L\) large enough to contain the affine function below.  Let
\(K(u)={\bf 1}\{|u|\leq 1\}\).  Take \(K_D=2\) and use the deterministic
donor split whose fold sizes differ by at most one, as permitted by the
estimator construction.  Since \(r=0\), the polynomial basis is
\(b_0(u)=1\); choose the admissible normalized-shape threshold
\(0<c_G\leq1\).  Let \(E_0\) be constant, set \(z_0=1/2\), and put
\(\mathcal Z_+=\{1/2\}\).

For each \(T\), let \(n_1=N=T^2\).  Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_T\) be independent
uniform random variables on \([0,1]\), and define
\[
m(x)=8+x-\frac12,
\qquad
Q_{ti}=m(X_t)+\frac12U_{ti},
\]
where the \(U_{ti}\)'s are independent Rademacher variables and are independent
of the complete design.  Thus
\[
0\leq Q_{ti}\leq16,\qquad
\mathbb E[Q_{ti}\mid X_t,E_0]=m(X_t),\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(Q_{ti}-m(X_t)\mid X_t,E_0)=\frac14\geq B^{-1}.
\]
The density of \(X_t\) is one.  Moreover, the calendar vectors
\(((X_t,U_{ti})_i)_{t=1}^T\) are independent over \(t\), so their conditional
absolute-regularity coefficients are zero and hence obey
\(\beta_P(k\mid E_0)\leq\beta_0\rho_0^k\) for every admissible
\(\beta_0>0\), \(0<\rho_0<1\).

Independently of the historical sample, let
\[
Z_j=\frac12+V_j,
\]
where the \(V_j\)'s are independent Rademacher variables.  Then
\[
\mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]=z_0,\qquad
\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid E_0)=1,\qquad
\mathbb E[|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid E_0]=1\leq B.
\]
Consequently donor replication, donor independence, ellipticity, and the stated
fourth-moment bound all hold.  Set \(X_t^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_t\), which verifies
exact observation of the training coordinates.

The local-modulus condition can be checked exactly.  For
\(0<\delta\leq\delta_0\), both \(z_0+u\) and \(z_0-u\) belong to \([0,1]\)
whenever \(|u|\leq\delta\), and
\[
\omega_P(\delta;z_0)
=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|m(z_0+u)-m(z_0)|
=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|u|
=\delta.
\]
Thus the two-sided modulus holds with exponent one and the displayed constants.
The affine \(m\) belongs to \(\mathcal H_1(1,L)\), the query is at least
\(\delta_0\) from the boundary, and
\(P\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\geq c_X\).

It remains to define the event outcomes.  Put
\[
G={\bf 1}\{X_1\leq1/4\},
\qquad B_i(0)=8,
\qquad B_i(1)=8+G,
\qquad B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_i(1).
\]
Define \(B_i(a,\mathbf a_{-i})=B_i(a)\), and define every historical potential
outcome \(Q_{ti}(a)\) to equal the displayed \(Q_{ti}\).  These definitions
give consistency, historical consistency, no spillovers, and limited
anticipation.  They also satisfy the support restrictions.  The buy-and-hold
construction is realized by taking \(W_{i,-1}=1\) and
\(R_{i0}(a)=B_i(a)-1>-1\), for then
\(W_{i,-1}\{1+R_{i0}(a)\}=B_i(a)\).

Because \(m(z_0)=8\), event transport follows from
\[
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E[B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]=8=m(z_0).
\]
Conditional on the complete design, each event outcome is a constant and the
historical error path of unit \(i\) is a function only of
\((U_{ti})_{t=1}^T\).  Those paths are independent across \(i\).  Hence the
required conditional cross-unit independence holds, and identical conditional
laws of the \(U_{ti}\)'s give within-site replication.  This verifies every
member property in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(1)\).

By the target definition and the fact that \(G\) is Bernoulli with probability
\(1/4\),
\[
\tau_n(z_0)
=\mathbb E[B_i(1)-B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=\mathbb E[G]=\frac14,
\qquad
\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}=8+G.
\]
We next control the fitted untreated mean.  Under the chosen split, every
complementary fold size satisfies \(m_k\asymp N=T^2\).  Projection onto \([0,1]\) is
nonexpansive and fixes \(z_0\), so
\[
\mathbb E[(\widetilde z_{1k}-z_0)^2\mid E_0]
\leq \mathbb E\!\left[
\left\{m_k^{-1}\sum_{j\notin k}V_j\right\}^2\right]
=m_k^{-1}=O(T^{-2}).
\]
The initial log-adjusted bandwidth in the feasible estimator is, for all large
\(T\),
\[
\underline h_T
=C_h\left[(Tn_1)^{-1/3}
\vee\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}
\vee N^{-1/2}\right]
=C_h\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T.
\]
Conditional on any \(\widetilde z_{1k}\in[0,1]\), the intersection of
\([\widetilde z_{1k}-\underline h_T,
\widetilde z_{1k}+\underline h_T]\) with \([0,1]\) has length at least
\(\underline h_T\).  Donor independence and the uniform design therefore give
\[
P\!\left\{
\sum_{t=1}^T K\!\left(\frac{X_t-\widetilde z_{1k}}
{\underline h_T}\right)=0
\,\middle|\,E_0,\widetilde z_{1k}\right\}
\leq(1-\underline h_T)^T
\leq e^{-T\underline h_T}.
\]
A union bound over the fixed number \(K_D\) of folds shows that the event
\(\mathcal A_T\), on which every initial window is nonempty, has probability
tending to one.  On a nonempty order-zero fit,
\(G_{1k}(h)/L_{1k}(h)=1\); hence the normalized-shape rule selects
\(h_{1k}=\underline h_T\) on \(\mathcal A_T\).

Let \(I_k=\{t:|X_t-\widetilde z_{1k}|\leq\underline h_T\}\).  On
\(\mathcal A_T\), the fold intercept is
\[
e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_{1k}
=\frac1{n_1|I_k|}\sum_{t\in I_k}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Q_{ti}.
\]
Its conditional-mean part differs from \(m(z_0)=8\) by at most
\(\underline h_T+|\widetilde z_{1k}-z_0|\), because \(m(x)-m(z_0)=x-z_0\).
Conditional on the design and donors, its error part has mean zero and variance
\[
\frac1{4n_1|I_k|}\leq\frac1{4n_1}.
\]
All order-zero successful intercepts lie in \([0,B]\), while a failed-fold
contribution is zero.  Combining the last three displays, using the donor
second-moment bound and \(P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\to0\), and then averaging
the fixed number of folds yields
\[
\mathbb E[(\widehat m_1-m(z_0))^2\mid E_0]\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=G-\frac14-\{\widehat m_1-m(z_0)\}.
\]
Since the final brace converges to zero in conditional \(L^2\), the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives
\[
\lim_{T\to\infty}
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
=\mathbb E[(G-1/4)^2]
=\frac{3}{16}.
\]

The four comparator terms are all exactly of order \(T^{-2}\):
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}=n_1^{-1}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sm}}=(Tn_1)^{-2/3}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}=T^{-2}.
\]
Thus \(R_\star=T^{-2}\).

For the event multiplier, all observed event outcomes equal \(8+G\), so
\[
E_{1i}=\frac1{n_1}
\{B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\}=0
\quad\text{for every }i.
\]
It follows identically that \(G_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\#}=0\) and
\(r_{\mathrm{tr}}=0\).  Nevertheless the centered event-average contribution is
\(\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]
=G-1/4\), whose conditional variance is \(3/16\).

Finally consider the interval in \(\texttt{def:honest-interval}\).  On every
successful order-zero fit, writing
\(I_k(h)=\{t:|X_t-\widetilde z_{1k}|\leq h_{1k}\}\), its weights satisfy
\[
a_{ti k}=\frac{{\bf 1}\{t\in I_k(h)\}}
{n_1|I_k(h)|},
\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^T a_{ti k}=\frac1{n_1},
\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^T|\bar a_{ti}|=\frac1{n_1}.
\]
Therefore, on successful fits,
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log\!\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}}\right)
\frac1{n_1}\right\}^{1/2}=O(T^{-1}),
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log\!\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}}\right)
\frac1{n_1}\right\}^{1/2}=O(T^{-1}).
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T\), nonnegativity and unit sum of the local-constant weights,
together with their kernel support, give
\[
A_L
\leq C_{0,1}L\,\underline h_T
=O\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right).
\]
Here \(D=1\), and
\[
M_4(m_k)=\frac{16}{m_k}
+3\left(1-\frac1{m_k}\right)\leq16.
\]
Since \(K_D\) and \(\alpha\) are fixed, this implies
\(q_k=O(1)\), \(\delta_k=O(m_k^{-1/2})=O(T^{-1})\), and hence
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}=O(T^{-1}),
\qquad
\max_k\delta_k\leq\delta_0
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  On \(\mathcal A_T\), all Gram matrices are
positive, all weights and radii are finite, and the finite donor sample
covariance admits the declared spectral clipping.  Thus the declared bad-sample
event is absent on \(\mathcal A_T\) for all large \(T\).  We have proved
\[
P(\text{bad sample}\mid E_0)\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
H_\alpha\,\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A_T}
=O\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)=o(1).
\]
Also \(\widehat\tau-G=8-\widehat m_1\to0\) in conditional probability.  Since
\(|G-1/4|\geq1/4\) almost surely, the event
\(\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\}\cap\mathcal A_T\) is contained, for all large
\(T\), in the union of
\(\{|\widehat\tau-G|\geq1/16\}\) and
\(\{H_\alpha\geq1/8\}\).  Both probabilities tend to zero, while
\(P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\to0\).  Hence
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\longrightarrow0,
\]
which completes all parts of the proposition.
